key_insight: The paper designs pull-based sampling policies that minimize the mean age of incorrect information (MAoII) when remotely estimating a Markov source, accounting for both estimation errors and how long they persist.
engineering_relevance: This provides a principled scheduling framework for edge monitoring systems where communication is limited and freshness matters more than raw update rate.
method: Models the source as a finite-state DTMC and the monitor as using a MAP estimator.
Formulates the zero-delay case as an SMDP to derive an optimal observation-dependent pull policy.
Handles the unit-delay case with belief-MDP modeling and a constrained deep reinforcement learning policy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical algorithms for computing MAoII and average sampling rate under a given policy, and uses these to optimize the system under a long-run sampling-rate constraint.
watch_item: The unit-delay setting relies on belief-state estimation and CDRL, which can be computationally heavy and sensitive to approximation errors.
paper_title: Minimizing Age of Incorrect Information in Pull-Based Remote Estimation of a Markov Source
